title: Hot Brown
subtitle: An open-face Kentucky baked sandwich with Mornay sauce and bacon
excerpt: Toast layered with sliced turkey and tomato, blanketed in a rich Mornay sauce, finished with bacon and baked until bubbling and golden. A Louisville diner classic that is a full meal on a single plate.
sourceNotes: Kentucky diner classic, originated at the Brown Hotel in Louisville. Adapted for a home oven.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the Mornay sauce up to a day ahead and refrigerate. Reheat gently before assembling.

content.text: The Hot Brown is an open sandwich baked under a Mornay sauce until the edges bubble and the bacon crisps. It is rich and filling and needs nothing alongside. The sauce must be made first and kept warm, as the whole dish assembles and bakes in minutes.
Heat the oven to 200C. Cook the bacon under a grill or in a dry frying pan until just cooked through but not yet crisp. Set aside.

Make the Mornay sauce. Melt the butter in a saucepan over a medium heat. Add the flour and stir constantly for 1 minute to make a roux. Add the warm milk gradually, whisking continuously to prevent lumps. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Remove from the heat and stir in the gruyere and cheddar until melted. Season with salt and pepper.
Place the toast slices in a roasting tin or individual oven-safe dishes. Lay the sliced turkey generously over each piece of toast.
Lay tomato slices over the turkey. Pour the Mornay sauce over each portion until the toast and turkey are completely covered. Scatter the parmesan over the top.
Lay the bacon rashers over the top of each portion.
Bake for 10 to 15 minutes until the sauce is bubbling and the edges are golden. Serve immediately in the dish.

items.cause: The milk was added too quickly or not whisked constantly.
items.fix: Add the milk in a thin stream while whisking hard, or pass the finished sauce through a sieve and reheat gently.

items.symptom: The toast goes soft and soggy.
items.cause: The toast was too thin or the sauce too watery.
items.fix: Use thick slices and a properly thickened sauce. The toast will absorb some sauce, which is part of the dish, but should hold its shape.

items.cause: The oven was not hot enough or the dish was placed too low.
items.fix: Bake on the top third of the oven, and finish under the grill for 2 minutes if needed for more colour.
